# User

This file describes the person who owns and runs this Zeno instance. Zeno reads it at boot and injects it into the system prompt — so it knows how to address you, what defaults to use for ambiguous queries, and which preferences to respect.

## Identity

- **Name:** <your-name>
- **GitHub username:** <your-github-username>
- **Slack user ID:** <your-slack-user-id>
- **Timezone:** <auto-detected-tz>

## Preferences

Free-form notes on how Zeno should communicate with you. Examples:

- Reply in Brazilian Portuguese by default; switch if I write in another language.
- Be direct, short answers, minimal preamble.
- Always confirm before any destructive operation (push --force, delete, drop, etc.).
- Use Slack markdown — code blocks for commands, bold for emphasis, no big tables.

## Context

Free-form notes about your work and projects so Zeno can give relevant answers without you re-explaining every time. Examples:

- Main personal project: `<repo>` (`<owner>/<repo>`).
- Day-job stack: TypeScript / React / Node, deployed to Vercel.
- Work GitHub organization: `<acme-corp>` — my PAT is SSO-authorized for it.
- I follow conventional commits; PR titles in imperative mood.
- Meetings on Mon/Wed mornings — avoid scheduling deep work then.

## What this file is NOT

- **Not credentials.** Tokens for Slack, GitHub, and Claude OAuth live in `.env`. Never put secrets in `USER.md`.
- **Not runtime config.** Log levels, ports, paths — also `.env`.
- **Not a list of allowlisted users.** When Zeno gains multi-user support, that will be a separate config (e.g., `ALLOWED_USERS` env or its own file).

## Loading behavior

If `USER.md` is missing at boot, Zeno still starts but logs a warning (`event: "user_md_missing"`) and operates without user-specific context. The system prompt simply omits the user section. This is fine for development; production (i.e., your daily-use Zeno) should always have `USER.md` populated.
